connectorUiConfig.title: MuleSoft CloudHub Logs (Push Connector via Codeless Connector Framework)
connectorUiConfig.descriptionMarkdown: Receive MuleSoft CloudHub application logs through the Azure Monitor Logs Ingestion API. Configure each application with a compatible custom asynchronous Log4j appender, or forward through an external collector that supports this API and the connector's schema. This connector deploys the receiving resources; it does not include a sender, discover applications, or call the CloudHub application/log APIs. Use the setup steps below to configure and validate your sender.

dataTypes.name: MuleSoftCloudhubLogs_CL
dataTypes.lastDataReceivedQuery:
MuleSoftCloudhubLogs_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(12h)
| summarize Time = max(TimeGenerated)
| where isnotempty(Time)

resourceProvider.permissionsDisplayText: Read and Write permissions are required.

customs.name: Microsoft.Insights/dataCollectionEndpoints
customs.description: Data Collection Endpoint is required for the modern push connector to receive data from the external security system.

customs.name: Microsoft.Insights/dataCollectionRules
customs.description: Data Collection Rule is required to define the schema and transformations for incoming data.

customs.name: Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments
customs.description: Role assignment is required to grant the Entra application permissions to send data to the Data Collection Rule.

instructionSteps.title: 1. Deploy the receiving resources
instructionSteps.description: Select Deploy to provision the receiving resources and obtain the configuration values below. Deployment does not configure MuleSoft applications or start forwarding logs. Your sender needs an Entra access token and Monitoring Metrics Publisher access on the DCR. See the [Logs Ingestion API overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/logs/logs-ingestion-api-overview).

parameters.content: Deploy the Log Analytics table, Data Collection Endpoint (DCE), Data Collection Rule (DCR), and Entra application with ingestion permissions.

parameters.label: Deploy MuleSoft CloudHub Logs receiving resources

parameters.content:
### Sender configuration

Copy these values into your compatible appender or external collector. The DCR value below is its immutable ID, not its ARM resource ID. Use Entra application credentials, not MuleSoft Connected App credentials.

parameters.text: Store the client secret in protected application or collector configuration. Do not hardcode it in log4j2.xml or include it in logs.

instructionSteps.title: 2. Configure application log forwarding
instructionSteps.description:
1. Choose a custom asynchronous Log4j appender that supports Azure Monitor Logs Ingestion, or send logs to an external collector that implements it. No ready-made sender is supplied with this connector; a generic HTTP appender alone does not implement Entra token refresh or schema mapping.
2. Add the appender dependency to your Mule application's `pom.xml` and configure `src/main/resources/log4j2.xml` using that appender's instructions. Repeat for each application, or use your deployment automation. Follow the guide for your platform: [CloudHub 1.0](https://docs.mulesoft.com/cloudhub/custom-log-appender) or [CloudHub 2.0](https://docs.mulesoft.com/cloudhub-2/ch2-integrate-log-system). Do not use the 1.0 file/appender configuration unchanged on 2.0.
3. Configure the sender with the tenant ID, client ID, protected client secret, DCE URL, DCR immutable ID and stream name from step 1. It must acquire and refresh an Entra token with scope `https://monitor.azure.com/.default`, then POST a JSON array to `{DCE}/dataCollectionRules/{DCR-immutable-ID}/streams/Custom-MuleSoftCloudhubLogs_CL?api-version=2023-01-01` with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and `Content-Type: application/json`.
4. Map records to the DCR fields: `EventTime` (UTC timestamp), `Level`, `Logger`, `Message`, `Thread`, `Exception`, `ApplicationDomainName`, `InstanceId`, `WorkerId`, `Environment`, `Region`, and `ApplicationData` (JSON object). Configure batching, retry/backoff and delivery monitoring in the sender. See [Logs Ingestion API examples](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/logs/tutorial-logs-ingestion-code).
5. Deploy a test application and verify forwarding before rolling out to other applications or disabling existing logging.

instructionSteps.title: 3. Verify ingestion
instructionSteps.description:
Generate a uniquely identifiable test log and confirm its message and application context in `MuleSoftCloudhubLogs_CL`:

```kusto
MuleSoftCloudhubLogs_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| project TimeGenerated, ApplicationDomainName, Level, Message
| take 10
```

If the record is missing, inspect sender delivery errors: check the Entra token for 401, DCR permissions for 403, and the stream name and JSON field types for 400. Confirm connectivity to the DCE and token endpoint. Receiving-resource deployment alone does not confirm end-to-end ingestion.
